raw_response:
I'm 59 this year, and I've been farming these 20 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. It's just me in the house now, so I have to be careful with both my body and my money — my back isn't what it used to be, and I need to keep some cash aside in case I get sick. I only finished primary school, but I know this land better than any book.

I plant wheat on 14 mu every year, and last October I put it in like always. I used about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer then. Now it's spring, and when the wheat starts jointing I need to topdress with about 30 jin of urea per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang tried using less fertilizer last year and his wheat turned yellow and thin — I'm not taking that chance. I'd rather spend a bit more than lose the crop. I'll irrigate three times: once now in spring, once right after the topdress at jointing, and once when the wheat flowers. I spray herbicide once in spring, and if I see aphids I'll spray insecticide. For harvest in early June I'll need to hire a couple of people to help, because six days to cut, thresh, and get the maize in is too much for just me.

The summer maize goes in right after the wheat comes off, mid-June. That window is tight — sometimes only five or six days — so I hire a tractor to plow and a machine to plant. I buy hybrid seed every year, costs about 55 yuan per mu. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 50 jin per mu, and if the rain is good I might topdress a bit of urea when the plants are knee-high. Two irrigations if it's dry — one when the seedlings are small, and one at flowering. I might hire help for planting since I'm not fast enough alone anymore.

I keep 6 mu for cotton. Cotton earns more money but the picking is backbreaking work. I plant in late April. I use about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and topdress with about 20 jin of urea once when the cotton starts flowering. Two irrigations. The real problem is picking in September and October — I have to hire people for about 10 days of labor, which costs me, but I cannot pick 6 mu of cotton by myself at my age.

I'm not changing much this year. Last year I got about 420 jin per mu of wheat, 450 jin of maize, and about 220 jin of cotton lint. I'll be happy with the same. I use a bit less fertilizer than what the extension people recommend, but after 35 years I know what this soil can do. I need to save money for doctor visits and hired labor. Better to be a little careful than sorry.
